item_name: Target-conditioned distractor-aware tracking with explicit target-absent handling (DiMP, PrDiMP, KeepTrack, ToMP, long-term trackers)

full_text_checked: Full text, including appendix and supplementary, extracted from the arXiv PDFs for DiMP v2, PrDiMP v1, KeepTrack v2 (supplementary A-G: data mining, architecture, Algorithm 1, search-area rescaling, Tables 9-16, failure cases), ToMP v1 (supplementary B: score maps, failure cases) and LTMU v1. For pytracking, only dimp50.py (thresholds) and the localize_advanced/track logic in dimp.py were checked. Not accessed: the LTMU code, the KeepTrack and ToMP code files, the original OxUvA and VOT-LT benchmark papers, and the CVF proceedings versions. The appearance features of the KeepTrack association network and the SuperGlue layers have no parameter counts in the paper, and none were computed from code.
task_and_output: All five works do generic single-object visual tracking. The target is specified only by a box in the first frame, and the tracker must locate this one instance in every later frame. DiMP: an online-learned convolutional target model (a 4x4 kernel on backbone block-3 features) gives a dense target-confidence score map over a search region; the box comes from a separate IoU-Net regressor. PrDiMP: the same, but each branch outputs a probability density over target centre and box (an energy-based density, trained with KL divergence to a Gaussian label density). KeepTrack: SuperDiMP score map, then extraction of target candidates (local maxima), a learned association of all candidates between consecutive frames (assignment matrix with dustbins for appeared or disappeared candidates), an object database with ids, the selected target object (or none) and a per-frame sample confidence beta. On OxUvA and VOT-LT it also outputs a presence score per frame, thresholded for present/absent. ToMP: a Transformer predicts the weights of the target classifier and the box regressor from training frames plus the test frame (transductive); outputs a score map and a box. LTMU: a long-term tracker whose output per frame is a box plus a verification-based found/not-found state. When the target is lost it runs global re-detection (Faster R-CNN candidates -> SiamRPN boxes -> RTMDNet verifier). A cascaded-LSTM meta-updater outputs a binary decision on whether to update the online tracker in this frame.
data_and_independent_videos: Training (all on videos disjoint from test): DiMP/PrDiMP train splits of LaSOT, GOT10k, TrackingNet and COCO (PrDiMP: 50 epochs x 1000 iterations). KeepTrack: base tracker frozen; association net trained on a train-train split of the LaSOT training set, with a train-val split held out, 15 epochs x 6400 sub-sequences. Frames mined from dumped tracker outputs (Table 9: 1.8M frames with a single candidate, 67.9%; 498k multi-candidate frames with correct selection, 18.4%; 76k frames with the target not detected, 2.8%; 42k frames detected but not selected, 1.5%). LTMU meta-updater: LaSOT training set, iterative training with K=3. ToMP: same training sets as DiMP family [uncertain: exact list not re-read]. Test (unseen videos, standard benchmark test splits): LaSOT test 280 videos, about 2500 frames on average; LaSOTExtSub 150 videos (15 classes x 10); OxUvA long-term test 166 videos, average 3300 frames, sparse 1 Hz labels with present/absent annotation, threshold set on a separate dev split (dataset total 366 tracks in 337 videos, per LTMU). VOT2018LT 35 sequences, 146,817 frames, on average 12 target disappearances of about 40 frames each. VOT2019LT/2020LT 50 sequences, 215,294 frames, on average 10 disappearances of about 52 frames. UAV123 123 videos; NFS (30 FPS version) 100 videos; OTB-100 100 videos; TrackingNet and GOT10k test servers. DiMP and PrDiMP ablations: a pooled OTB-100+NFS+UAV123 set of 323 videos, average of 5 runs. KeepTrack ablations: NFS, UAV123 and LaSOT, average of 5 runs. LTMU ablations: LaSOT test. Note: the ablations are run on test sets, so there is no separate validation split for ablation choices.
target_size_and_input_resolution: DiMP: search region 5 x target size, resized to 288x288 (18*16), stride-16 features, so the score map is 18x18 and the target spans about 3-4 score cells. The other 14-15 cells are background used as negatives. SuperDiMP: search scale 6, 352x352 crop, 22x22 score map. KeepTrack: search scale 8, 480x480 crop, 30x30 score map, candidates are 5x5 max-pool local maxima with score >= 0.05. ToMP: search scale 5 and 18x18 score map (Sec. A.2 of its supplement). LTMU verifier: 107x107 patches. The input is RGB natural video of arbitrary resolution (LaSOT, OxUvA from YouTube). Target sizes in pixels are not limited and include small objects in UAV123 and LaSOTExtSub. In all these trackers the target occupies only about 1/5-1/8 of the search-crop width.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: The benchmarks are mostly 30 fps consumer, YouTube or UAV video. NFS is used in its 30 FPS version. OxUvA labels are sparse at 1 Hz, but tracking runs on all frames. There is free camera motion, including handheld and UAV cameras, background clutter and scale change. No compensation of self-motion is used beyond moving the search window to the last estimate. Tracker speeds: DiMP 43 FPS (ResNet-50) and 57 FPS (ResNet-18) on a GTX 1080; PrDiMP about 30/40 FPS; KeepTrack 18.3 FPS and KeepTrackFast 29.6 FPS on a 2080Ti; ToMP-50 24.8 FPS and ToMP-101 19.6 FPS; LTMU about 13 FPS.
detector_and_exemplar: No class-specific detector in DiMP, PrDiMP, KeepTrack or ToMP. The exemplar is the first-frame box: 15 augmented samples initialise the DiMP memory. The memory then grows with confidently tracked frames up to 50 samples (oldest discarded; KeepTrack instead discards the sample with the lowest age x confidence). ToMP uses the first frame plus the most recent confident frame as training frames. LTMU uses a Faster R-CNN generic detector only for global re-detection after loss, then SiamRPN and an RTMDNet verifier against the target template.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: DiMP: offline meta-learning of the backbone (ResNet-18/50), the model initializer, the steepest-descent optimizer and the discriminative loss itself (target mask m_c, spatial weight v_c, regularisation lambda and label y_c). The online loss is least squares near the target plus a hinge max(0, s) on background, so easy negatives can score very negative. The authors note that calibrated target confidences near the target help detecting target loss. The target filter is fitted online per sequence: 10 steepest-descent steps on the first frame, then 2 steps every 20 frames or 1 step when a distractor peak is detected. PrDiMP: same nodes. The training loss is KL divergence to a Gaussian label density (target centre: sigma 1/4 target size; box: sigma 0.05), with grid or Monte Carlo approximation; the online optimizer uses a second-order Taylor expansion. KeepTrack: base tracker frozen. Trained parts: a 2x2 conv on 1024-channel ResNet-50 block-3 features (to 256 channels), an MLP for score and position (3->32->64->128->256 with BN), a SuperGlue GNN (2 self- plus 2 cross-attention layers, then a 1x1 conv) and Sinkhorn (10 iterations) with dustbins. Loss: L_sup (NLL of the annotated target correspondence, with simulated occlusion and re-detection mapped to dustbins) plus L_self (NLL on synthetic augmented copies of the same frame's candidates). Adam, learning rate 1e-4. No parameter count is given. ToMP: Transformer encoder-decoder model predictor, learned foreground and test embeddings and a target-extent MLP, trained end-to-end. LTMU: matching network (ResNet-50) trained separately; response-map subnetwork, three-stage cascaded LSTM (64 units, time steps 20/8/3) and 2 FC layers. The binary label is IoU > 0.5 for 'can update' and IoU = 0 for 'cannot'; IoU values between 0 and 0.5 are excluded. Parameter counts are not reported in any of the five papers.
controls_seeds_splits: Seeds and runs: DiMP, PrDiMP, KeepTrack and ToMP report the average of 5 tracking runs (the tracker is stochastic) but give no confidence intervals and no per-video paired tests. Training-seed variation is not reported. Matched ablations: DiMP Table 1: only the initializer (target-only exemplar, Siamese-like) vs gradient descent vs steepest descent with background. Table 2 adds components one at a time. Table 3: no update vs model averaging vs memory-based update. PrDiMP Table 1: four regression losses applied to each branch separately. KeepTrack Table 10 (one component at a time, including base, memory confidence, larger search area and rescaling), Table 11 (no GNN, i.e. only feature encoding plus Sinkhorn, vs 2 or 9 GNN layers), Table 2 (L_sup vs L_self vs both, with and without data mining) and Table 3 (memory weighting). ToMP Table 1 (encodings), Table 3 (only initial frame vs initial plus previous frame) and Table 4 (swapping the DiMP optimizer for the ToMP predictor). LTMU Tables 5-7 (time step, input removal, training iterations), Fig. 9 (four trackers with and without the meta-updater) and Table 9 (update precision, recall and TNR). Splits: test videos are unseen in training. OxUvA presence threshold is tuned on the dev split (KeepTrack). There is no ablation that isolates absent-frame detection quality on OxUvA or VOT-LT in any of these papers.

tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (standard test splits for all five). Target absence: yes for KeepTrack and LTMU on OxUvA (TNR on absent frames) and VOT-LT (F-score over presence thresholds). DiMP, PrDiMP and ToMP report no absence metric; DiMP and PrDiMP have only a code-level 'not_found' flag when the peak is < 0.25. Similar distractors: yes. KeepTrack is designed for this and reports UAV123 'Similar Object' and LaSOT 'Background Clutter' attributes; DiMP handles distractor peaks in code ('hard_negative' and 'uncertain' flags); ToMP failure analysis shows distractors are the main failure mode. Occlusion: yes (Full and Partial Occlusion attributes; VOT-LT disappearances; KeepTrack search-area rescaling at occlusion). Night or low light: not reported separately; only the 'Illumination Variation' attribute in LaSOT and UAV123 is shown. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes; all are causal online trackers that update their memory from their own predictions, and LTMU and KeepTrack explicitly gate those updates. Multi-object setting with an external detector and association (MOT): not tested. KeepTrack notes that MOT differs because it associates only tracker-defined candidates of one target.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanisms: (a) Discriminative target model from exemplars (DiMP). A small linear filter (4x4 x C) over local features is fitted per sequence by a few steepest-descent steps on a ridge loss. The target neighbourhood is regressed to a Gaussian label and background is penalised only by a hinge on positive scores. Training samples are the first frame (augmented) plus later confident frames. Using background negatives instead of only target appearance gave +5.6 AUC on 323 videos (58.2 -> 63.8). Memory updates added +2.1 (61.7 -> 63.8). (b) Distractor-aware confidence (DiMP code). Find the main peak, mask a neighbourhood of 2.2 target sizes, and find the second peak. If the second peak is above 0.8 x the main peak, use displacement from the previous position to choose; if still ambiguous, flag 'uncertain' and do not update. If the main peak is < 0.25, report 'not found': keep the position and do not update. (c) Probabilistic score (PrDiMP). The score map is a density trained by KL divergence to a label density, which gives a probabilistic meaning to confidence. The paper shows AUC gains but does not measure calibration. (d) Candidate association with explicit 'disappeared' or 'new' (KeepTrack). Candidates are local maxima with score >= 0.05. Each candidate gets features (score, position, appearance), a GNN mixes them with neighbouring candidates, and Sinkhorn matching with dustbins runs between consecutive frames. Ids persist, and an ambiguous match (< 0.75) is reset. The target is kept by id. If the target id vanishes, the tracker re-detects only when the best candidate score is >= 0.25. It switches from the current target to another candidate only if that candidate's score exceeds every past score of the current target. Sample confidence (sqrt of max score if the id is preserved, else max score) gates memory updates (ignore < 0.5). The presence threshold is set on a dev split. The association added +1.3 LaSOT AUC over the same tracker. Even without the GNN, the feature encoding plus matching recovered +0.8 of it. (e) Learned update gating (LTMU). A temporal LSTM over the last 20 frames of box, score, response map and appearance score predicts 'safe to update'. This raises update precision from 0.867 to 0.952 and update TNR from 0.479 to 0.862, and adds +3.3 LaSOT success. Proposed modification (ours, not published): a FlyVis readout node that fits a tiny per-track discriminative filter on FlyVis output-cell activity from the 4 exemplar observations, using neighbours in the crop as hard negatives. It would then compute a peak-ratio and displacement ambiguity test and refuse when ambiguous or when the main peak is low. Details are in candidate_node_change.
transfer_limits: 1) Context ratio: these trackers see a search crop of 5-8 target sizes, and the target is only about 3-4 of 18-30 score cells, so most of the crop gives background and distractor negatives. Our eye crop is max(2 x larger side, 64 px). The median target is 9.37 x 12.06 lattice steps inside a 721-hexal disc about 31 columns across, so there is little background and often only partial neighbours. This limits the DiMP background-negative gain (the +5.6 AUC came with plenty of background) and the KeepTrack peak-pair logic (a second distinct peak needs room). Mitigation would require a larger crop, which changes the FlyVis input. 2) Feature strength: DiMP and KeepTrack rely on ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 block-3 features (1024 channels, RGB) fine-tuned end-to-end on about 4 large datasets. FlyVis gives 34 output cell types per column computed from grey luminance, trained for optic flow. Appearance identity is weak, so motion and position cues must carry discrimination. KeepTrack itself says position cues fail when similar objects cross (Fig. 7). 3) Exemplar quantity: DiMP initialises from 15 augmented samples and keeps up to 50, while we have 4 recent tracker observations that may already be contaminated. LTMU shows that update gating matters a lot (update TNR 0.48 -> 0.86). 4) Rate: 30 Hz matches the benchmarks, but our crop moves and rescales with the track prediction, so FlyVis temporal state is not aligned with a fixed world frame, unlike a CNN on a single frame. 5) Our refusal must decide whether a corrected centre is better than the Kalman/ByteTrack prediction. OxUvA TNR and VOT-LT F-score evaluate presence, not usefulness of a correction, and none of these papers evaluate calibration (no ECE or reliability plots). Their thresholds (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.8) are tuned on their score scales and do not transfer. 6) Environment: the YOLO detector plus ByteTrack/MASA already does detection-level association. KeepTrack-style association is essentially what ByteTrack/MASA do, so by the project boundary it would be a tracker change, not a FlyVis modernization, unless the association features come from FlyVis and FlyVis beats no-FlyVis features in the same matcher. 7) Gains in these papers are +1 to +6 AUC on SOT benchmarks, averaged over 5 runs, with no confidence intervals. Our earlier MASA spatial version moved HOTA only 61.6548 -> 61.6727 (not confirmed), so small single-object gains may not show up in HOTA.
research_questions_addressed: Q1 (direct evidence, engineering not insect): DiMP Table 1 shows that exemplar-only matching (58.2) is clearly worse than discriminative fitting with background negatives (63.8). KeepTrack shows that explicitly tracking distractors with a 'disappeared' option and conservative re-detection or switching rules adds +1.3 LaSOT AUC and the best OxUvA MaxGM (80.9), including absent frames (TNR 81.2). There is no connectome or insect evidence here. Q2 (design analogy): DiMP Table 2 separates the gains: loss learning (+0.5), extra classification block (+0.7) and backbone fine-tuning (+2.6). The backbone (representation) gave the largest gain. This suggests separating readout-fitting gains from core-training gains with the same additive protocol on our B/C/D variants. Q3 (caution): the evidence is 30 fps natural video, but with 5-8x context crops and RGB deep features, unlike our 2x crop and 721 grey hexals. Q4 (direct design evidence): KeepTrack (memory confidence beta, ignore < 0.5: +1.5 LaSOT) and LTMU (a learned gate whose label is localisation correctness, IoU > 0.5 vs IoU = 0, excluding the ambiguous middle) show that a separately trained 'is this result correct' decision improves which own predictions are trusted. This is the closest analogue to our usefulness-aligned intervention score. PrDiMP gives a probabilistic score but shows no calibration result. Q5 (design input): the cheapest transferable parts are the online ridge-plus-hinge filter fit (no extra learned parameters, a few conjugate or steepest-descent steps) and the peak-ratio ambiguity rule; both fit within an ~11k readout.
candidate_node_change: Node: the FlyVis activity readout (read-out node of the fly path, allowed by the project boundary). Change: replace the learned exemplar-attention readout with a 'discriminative exemplar filter' readout in the style of DiMP. Input: FlyVis output activity at the last T steps for 721 columns. A learned 1x1 projection takes 34 cell types to C=16 channels (about 560 parameters), followed by a 7-hexal neighbourhood pooling. Per track and per loss event, fit a filter w (7 x 16 = 112 weights) by 5 steepest-descent steps on the 4 exemplar crops. The label is a Gaussian at the recorded centre with sigma = 1/4 target size. The loss is least squares within the target mask plus hinge max(0, s) elsewhere, and columns covered by other YOLO detections in the crop are up-weighted as hard negatives. Learn offline only the mask, spatial weight, regulariser and label shape (a few dozen parameters, DiMP '+Loss') plus the projection, through the frozen or trained FlyVis core. Decision: score map s = w * features. Let p1 be the main peak and p2 the second peak outside 2.2 target radii. Refuse if p1 < tau_found. If p2 > rho x p1, choose by displacement from the prediction, and refuse if still ambiguous (DiMP 'uncertain'). Otherwise propose the centre correction. Optional usefulness head (LTMU-like, Q4): a logistic head on [p1, p2/p1, displacement, peak sharpness, exemplar-fit residual] trained on train104 with label 'corrected error < predicted error' (excluding near-ties). tau and rho are set on train26 or dev35 only. Controls (rule 6.16 three-way): (1) stand without correction; (2) the same filter readout on a non-FlyVis feature map of equal size: raw grey hexal luminance plus frame difference, or the existing B network features (~9.6k parameters), with identical exemplars, history, fitting steps and thresholds selected the same way; (3) the same with stock frozen FlyVis (C); (4) optionally with trained FlyVis (D). A FlyVis result requires (3) or (4) to beat (2). Minimal check (offline, no HOTA run): on cached loss episodes from dev35, compare useful-correction precision in the top 1 percent and top 5 percent, and refusal TNR on frames where the previous target is outside the crop or occluded, against the current readout (7 of 37 useful in the top 1 percent). Use a paired bootstrap over videos. Stop condition, written before the run: stop this implementation if (3) does not beat (2) on useful-correction precision at matched coverage with a video-bootstrap 95 percent CI above 0, or if it does not exceed the current readout's 7/37 in the top 1 percent on dev35. Per rule 6.15, the replaceable failure nodes would then be the context size (crop scale 2 -> 4) or the feature projection, not the whole line. Only if the offline check passes, run one HOTA evaluation with MASA, three-way.
strongest_objection: These mechanisms work in their papers because the features are strong appearance descriptors (fine-tuned ResNet-50 on millions of RGB frames) and the search crop holds plenty of background (5-8 target sizes). The per-sequence discriminative fit and the peak-pair test then separate target from distractors. Our FlyVis output is a 34-type grey motion representation trained on optic flow, in a crop only 2x the target. So a DiMP-style filter on FlyVis features may reduce to a motion or position prior that the Kalman prediction and ByteTrack/MASA already provide. If control (2), the same filter on raw luminance or B features, matches (3), the gain is a readout or tracker improvement, not a FlyVis result. KeepTrack's own failure cases (crossing similar objects) are exactly our hard cases, and its gains are +1 to +4 SOT AUC averaged over 5 runs without confidence intervals, an effect size that our HOTA measurements have repeatedly been unable to resolve.
evidence_strength: Moderate to strong for the engineering claims. All five are peer-reviewed conference papers (ICCV 2019, CVPR 2020, ICCV 2021, CVPR 2022; LTMU CVPR 2020 [uncertain]) with public code; pytracking was verified and the DiMP thresholds were read from the code. The results have been reproduced and used as baselines by many later trackers on the same public benchmarks. Weaknesses: ablations are run on test sets, use averages of 5 runs without confidence intervals, and no paper measures confidence calibration. Absence handling is evaluated only through OxUvA and VOT-LT aggregate scores, with no ablation isolating the absence decision. Transfer to FlyVis features is untested, so the evidence for our decision is a design analogy only (weak).
